en: *לֶבֶס m. (λέβης; compare, however, לֶפֶס) caldron. Kelim XIV, 1 (Variant לפס); Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 1 הל׳ כדי וכ׳ the caldron (if defective) must be capable of serving as a receptacle for cups (in order to be fit for uncleanness).—plural לְבִיסִין. Sifré Bamidbar 158 לכוסין (correct accordingly; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Zutr. Matt., p. 279 ed. Bub. לפוסין); see לְבִיסַיָּא.

חֲטִיפָה f. (חָטַף) pinching off the rough edges. Kelim XIV, 1 מחוסר ח׳ (ed. Dehr. חֲטָפָה, Variant הֲגָפָה) a fragment of a vessel needing &c. in order to be used; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 1 הטפה, see הֲשָׁפָה.
לְטִישָׁה f. (לָטַשׁ) hammering, furbishing. Kelim XIV, 1 (Hai G.: לטיסא); Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 1.

מֵיחַם m. (חָמַם) vessel for heating water, boiler for mixing wine. Shabbat III, 5 המ׳ שפינהו וכ׳, explained ib. 41ᵃ, sq. המ׳ שפינה ממנו מים חמין a boiler which was emptied of its hot water; (oth. explanation) המ׳ שפינהו וכ׳ a boiler which has been removed from the stove; Yerushalmi ib. III, beginning 5ᶜ העביר את המ׳ when he has removed the boiler. Pesachim VII, 13 המ׳ באמצע the boiler for mixing the wine is placed between the two parties. Kelim XIV, 1; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 1 המ׳ כדי לקבל סלעין a boiler (when defective) is susceptible of uncleanness as long as it can be used for keeping coins in it; and from

מַתֶּכֶת f. (נָתַךְ) [molten] metal. Kelim XIII, 6 עץ המשמש את המ׳ the wooden part of a utensil which is subservient to the metallic participle Ib. 7 עשאו של מ׳ he replaced it by a metallic tooth; and see from—plural מַתָּכוֹת.—כְּלֵי מ׳ metallic vessels, utensils, tools &c. Ib. XIV, 1. Chullin I, 6; and see from

comments.en: Oversized metal vessels, such as oversized chests, arks, and cupboards, are impure (i.e., susceptible to impurity). [Those] such as as a table, or a slab, or a delphica (a three-legged table) of metal, are impure, and their minimum size [for purposes of impurity] is a handbreadth. They stated a general rule: A metal vessel which lacks the trimming [of its rough edges] is impure, and one that lacks polishing is pure, the words of Rabbi Akiva (Kel. 14:1), and the Sages say, [as to] metal vessels that became defective, if from the start they can be used for the general nature of their [intended] work, they are impure, and if not, they are pure. How so? A bucket: if it is capable of being filled [with water] to drink from it. A kettle: if it is capable of being heated to drink from it. And a cauldron: if it is capable of serving guests with it. A washbasin: if it is capable of putting one foot inside it. [If] they punctured a small kettle, [it is impure if it the hole is] large enough to have hot water poured into it. [If they punctured a regular-sized] kettle, large enough to receive selas. A cauldron: Large enough to receive ladles. Ladles: Large enough to receive perutahs inside them. The measure of [containers of] wine and oil: Their size [for purposes of impurity] is that of liquids, and Rabbi Eliezer says, of perutahs. A candle: Its size [for purposes of impurity] is that of liquids, and Rabbi Eliezer says, of perutahs.
comments.he: כלי מתכות הבאות במדה כגון השידה התיבה והמגדל הבאין במדה טמאין כגון השולחן והטבלא והדולפקי של מתכת טמאים ושיעורן בטפח כלל אמרו כלי מתכת המחוסר השפה טמא המחוסר לטישה טהור דברי ר' עקיבה וחכמים אומרים כלי מתכות שנתרועעו אם משמשין מעין מלאכתן ראשונה טמאין ואם לאו טהורין. כיצד דלי כדי למלאות בו לשתות. המיחם כדי להחם בו לשתות. והקיתון כדי לשמש בו את האורחין. ספל כדי להדיח בו <את> אחת מרגליו. נקבו קומקמין כדי לקבל חמין מיחם כדי לקבל סלעים הלבס כדי לקבל קיתונות. קיתונות כדי לקבל בו פרוטות. מדות היין והשמן שיעורן במשקין ורבי אליעזר אומר בפרוטות נר שיעורו במשקין ור' אליעזר אומר בפרוטות.

sections.en: What is the minimum size of [broken] metal vessels [for them to be susceptible to impurity]? A bucket must be of such a size as to draw water with it. A kettle must be such as water can be heated in it. A boiler, such as can hold selas. A cauldron, such as can hold jugs. Jugs, such as can hold perutahs. Wine-measures, such as can measure wine; and oil-measures, such as can measure oil. Rabbi Eliezer says: the size for all these is such as can hold perutahs. Rabbi Akiva says: a vessel that lacks trimming is susceptible to impurity, but one that lacks polishing is clean.
sections.he: כְּלֵי מַתָּכוֹת, כַּמָּה הוּא שִׁעוּרָן. הַדְּלִי, כְּדֵי לְמַלֹּאת בּוֹ. קֻמְקוּם, כְּדֵי לֵיחֵם בּוֹ. מֵחַם, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל סְלָעִים. הַלֶּפֶס, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל קִיתוֹנוֹת. קִיתוֹנוֹת, כְּדֵי לְקַבֵּל פְּרוּטוֹת. מִדּוֹת יַיִן, בְּיַיִן. וּמִדּוֹת שֶׁמֶן, בְּשָׁמֶן. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר, כֻּלָּן בִּפְרוּטוֹת. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, הַמְחֻסָּר חֲטִיפָה, טָמֵא. וְהַמְחֻסָּר לְטִישָׁה, טָהוֹר:

en: חַזְיָנָא, חַזְיָינָא m. Chaldaic (חזי, compare חָזִיז, חֲזִיזָא &c.) prickly bur, chestnut. Kelim XIV, 2 a cane with a metal knob כמין ח׳ (ed. Dehr. חזינה) of the shape of a chestnut bur (as a weapon).

חָבַל (Biblical Hebrew; compare חבב)
1) to seize, to take a pledge. Mekhilta Beshalach, Vayassa, section (Parashah) 1, and e., see חֲבוֹלָה.—Bava Metzia IX, 13 (115ᵃ) החוֹבֵל את הריחים he who seizes millstones (for his debt); and from

—2) to twist (see חֶבֶל); to do violence, unshape; to inflict a wound, to hurt (followed by ב of the object). Bava Kamma VIII, 1 החוֹבֵל בחבירו he who injures his neighbor. Shabbat XIV, 1. Ib. 106ᵃ חובל בצריך לכלבו one who wounds (an animal on the Sabbath is guilty) when he needs the blood for his dog. Ib. חובל בעלמא one who wounds generally (not for a purpose); and from

—3) to writhe, travail, see Piël

Nifal - נֶחְבַּל
1) to be seized. Yalkut Shemot 351 שניתן לֵיחָבֵל ביום (Bava Metzia 114ᵇ לַחֲבוֹל) which may be seized as a pledge in day time.

—2) to be injured. Tosefta Bava Kamma IX, 29 אע"פ שלא … מן הנֶחְבָּל וכ׳ although the injurer does not ask the injured (to pray for him), the injured must pray &c.; and from

Piël - חִיבֵּל
1) to injure, wound; to unshape, ruin, spoil. Berakhot 51ᵃ יש לי … לחַבֵּל I have permission to injure (kill). Bava Kamma 91ᵇ לחַבֵּל בעצמו to mutilate one’s self.—Kelim XIV, 2 משיְחַבֵּל from the moment he batters (the tube, for fitting it into the top of the staff); Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 5 משיִחְבּוֹל, see חָבַר. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 10 (play on חִבֵּל, Mishlei XXIII, 34) שחִבְּלָתוֹ יעל וכ׳ whom Jael mutilated on his head. Yalkut Shemot 301 חִבַּלְתֶּם מעשיכם you have ruined (turned to evil) your deeds. Sanhedrin 24ᵃ מְחַבְּלִין זה לזה וכ׳ (Manuscript Karlsruhe זה את זה) wound each other’s feelings in discussions; and from

—2) to travail. Taanit 8ᵃ bottom of page מְחַבֶּלֶת ואינה יולדת (Rashi: חוֹבֶלֶת) travails but cannot give birth.—Pass. pass. מְחוּבָּל ruined. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 30.

Hithpaël - הִתְחַבֵּל to be spoiled, ruined. Mekhilta Beshalach, Vayassa, section (Parashah) 1 נותן דבר המְחַבֵּל לתוך דבר המִתְחַבֵּל he puts a thing which spoils (the taste) into a thing which is spoiled.

חָבַר (Biblical Hebrew)
1) to join, befriend, assist. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. I, 39ᵇ top (reference. to Psalms LVIII, 6) [read:] כל מי שהיה חוֹבְרוֹ הוא חוברו whoever assisted him (in his political ambition), him he befriended.—Esp. חוֹבֵר, plural חוֹבְרִים, חוֹבְרִין having a share in the ownership of a sacrifice, see חֲבוּרָה. Menachot IX, 9 (93ᵇ bottom of page) אחד מניף לכל החו׳ Manuscript Munich (ed. חֲבֵרִים) one of the company does the waving in behalf of all of them. Ib. 94ᵃ נתמעטה בחו׳ is reduced in numbers as regards the participants (only one of them being required to act). Temurah 2ᵃ; Arakhin 2ᵃ בעלי ח׳ (subaudi קרבן) partners of a sacrifice (also בעלי קרבן).

—2) with על (compare זָוַג) to join against, protest. Bava Batra 11ᵃ חָבְרוּ עליו וכ׳ his brothers &c. combined to protest against his actions.

—3) to tie, fascinate, charm. Eicha Rabbah to I, 5 מביאין חוֹבֵר וחוֹבְרִין וכ׳ they procure a charmer and charm the serpent. Sifré Devarim 172 ה׳ מרובה he who charms large objects; Keritot 3ᵇ ח׳ גדול; Sanhedrin 65ᵃ חַבָּר גדול. Keritot l. common gender. חוֹבֵר חֶבֶר דבלאו הדין הוא but what kind of charmer (Devarim XVIII, 11) is he that is liable only to lashes (see לַאו)?; and from—[
4) (compare חָבַל) to unshape, wound. Denom. חַבּוּרָה.]

Piël - חִיבֵּר
1) to join, fasten. Yalkut Job 927 (reference. to Job XL, 30) מי שח׳ עצמו במצות whoever befriended himself with good deeds; Midrash Tanḥuma Nitsab. 4 (correct accordingly). Kelim XIV, 2 וחִבְּרָהּ לו (or וחֲבָרָהּ) and he fastened the tube to it (the staff). Ib. משיְחַבֵּר from the moment he attaches it, opposed משיחבל, see חָבַל.—Part. pass. מְחוּבָּר. Ib. XII, 2 כל המ׳ וכ׳ whatever is fastened (belonging) to an object fit to become unclean &c.—מ׳ (לקרקע) fixed, immovable, opposed תלוש. Bava Metzia 89ᵃ אוכל במ׳ may eat of what is standing in the field (Devarim XXIII, 25, sq.). Peah IV, 1, see דָּלִית. Yerushalmi ib. 18ᵃ ואינו מ׳ and when the Mishnah says בדלית ובדקל, it does not mean במ׳ בדלית וכ׳ ‘of that which is attached to the vine and tree’; אין תימר מ׳ הוא וכ׳ if you say, it means that which is attached, then the Mishnah means to say that the owner must designate the Peah while it is up (on the tree) &c.—Ib. II, beginning 16ᵈ (in a passage misplaced and corrupted) הא גדר מ׳ ואינו מ׳ this ‘fence’ (Mishnah ib. II, 3) is to be considered as something attached to the ground (like a growth) and (in other respects) as not attached.

—2) to charm. Eicha Rabbah, introduction (R. Joshua 2) התחיל מְחַבֵּר חֲבָרִים (not מחבי חביים) he began to consult charmers (with reference. to Ezekiel XXI, 26). Sanhedrin 65ᵃ מקטר לחַבֵּר he burns incense for charming purposes (to exorcise the demons); and from

Nifal - נֶחְבַּר to be joined, gathered. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 80 (reference. to Hosea VI, 9) as the priests נֶחְכָּרִים על וכ׳ are grooped around &c.; Makkot 10ᵃ מִתְחַבְּרִין וכ׳.

Hithpaël - הִתְחַבֵּר,

Nithpaël - נִתְחַבֵּר
1) same
; see supra.—2) to associate, make friends with. Pirkei Avot I, 7.—Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 20, beginning נִתְחַבְּרוּ מואב וכ׳
Moab and Midian formed an alliance; Midrash Tanḥuma Balak 3.—3) to be charmed, spellbound. Ib. Beshalach 18 מיד נתח׳ וכ׳ at once the bird is spellbound (by the snake looking at its shadow) and falls to pieces; Yalkut Shemot 255 מת (read מתחבר); Mekhilta Beshalach, Vayassa, section (Parashah) 1 מִתְחַבֵּר על צלו (not ומת׳ אל) it remains spell-bound over its own shadow.

מֵינֶקֶת, מֵנֶיקֶת f. (Biblical Hebrew; יָנַק)
1) a woman giving such, wet-nurse, see יָנַק.

—2) (see אָנַק) siphon, tube; small cup. Kelim IX, 2. Pirkei Avot Zar. 58ᵃ קדח במ׳ tapped with a siphon. Kelim XIV, 2 עשה בראשו מ׳ if he put a knob (cup) on the top of the cane. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 5 מיניקות שעשאה לתחת וכ׳ ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim XIV, 2 מניקת) a cup which one put under a door (as a pivot). Tosefta Demai III, 6 מניקית ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta); Yerushalmi ib. II, 22ᵈ bottom of page מניקת.—Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. IV, 44ᵇ top מיניקת.—[Pirké d’R. El. Chaldaic XLIII מ׳ ראשו, see מָנִיכָה.]—plural מֵינִיקִיּוֹת, מֵנִ׳. Tosefta Zevachim I, 12 בין במ׳ ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (ed. מֵנִיקוֹת) or when he made the libation out of tubes.—V. מְנַקִּיּוֹת.

נוֹי, נוֹא m. (נָוָה, נָאָה)
1) beauty, ornament. Kelim XIV, 2 עשאן לנוי (ed. Dehr. לנוֹאי) he attached them for ornamentation. Yevamot 39ᵇ הכונס את יבמתו … לשם נ׳ he who married his deceased brother’s wife (see יְבָמָה) for her beauty (not with the intention of perpetuating his brother’s name). Yerushalmi Ma'asrot III, end, 51ᵃ לנוֹיָיהּ של חצר to embellish the court. Zevachim 54ᵇ (play on בנוית, I Samuel XIX, 18) עוסקין בנוֹיוֹ של וכ׳ engaged in the embellishment of the world (consulting about building the Temple). Kohelet Rabbah to II, 12 והוא נוֹאוֹ and this (the nose) is man’s beauty; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 12 נאה (correct accordingly). Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 31 בעלת נ׳ a handsome woman; and from—plural נוֹיוֹת. Yalkut Song of Songs 988 בנוֹיוֹתָיו (not בנויתיו), see נָאֶה.

—2) נוֹי or נְוָיי (= נָוֶוה II) dwelling, climate. Bava Batra 24ᵇ משום נויי העיר because of the health of the town (which suffers from trees; Rashi: because of the beauty of the town which requires an open space all around); Yerushalmi ib. II, 13ᶜ top שניאו רע; Yerushalmi Sheviit VI, 36ᶜ bottom of page נִיוְיָהּ, see נָוֶה II.

סָמַר [(b. h.) to stand erect, bristle.—Denom. מַסְמֵר; whence סָמַר] to nail, fasten. Yerushalmi Megillah IV, 75ᶜ bottom of page זְמָרוֹ he nailed it (against the door, in an inappropriate place).

Piël - סִימֵּר to stud with nails. Kelim XIV, 2.—Part. pass. מְסוּמָּר. Shabbat VI, 2, and from סנדל המס׳ a nail-studded shoe.

comments.en: If a sheet that was susceptible to midras uncleanness made into a curtain, it becomes clean from midras uncleanness but it is still susceptible to corpse uncleanness. When does it become insusceptible to [midras] uncleanness? Bet Shammai says: when the loops have been tied to it. . Bet Hillel says: when it has been attached. Rabbi Akiva says: when it has been fixed.
comments.he: סָדִין שֶׁהוּא טְמֵא מִדְרָס וַעֲשָׂאוֹ וִילוֹן, טָהוֹר מִן הַמִּדְרָס, אֲבָל טָמֵא טְמֵא מֵת. מֵאֵימָתַי הִיא טָהֳרָתוֹ. בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיִּתָּבֵר. בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיִּקָּשֵׁר. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיִּקָּבֵעַ:

comments.en: A [wooden] staff to which one attached a nail at the top (lit., "head") for the sake of taking hold of the threshing floor is pure, but if it is so that the ground will not wear away [the staff], it is impure. [If] he attached [a nail] to the top for the sake of striking with it, it is impure. For ornamentation, it is pure. Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok says, [if] it had one row (דור) [of nails], it is impure, and two rows, it is pure. A whip to which one attached a nail at the top for the sake of striking with it is impure. For ornamentation, it is pure.
comments.he: מקל שעשה בראשו [מסמר] להיות תופם בו במקום הדייש טהור ואם בשביל שלא תהא הארץ אוכלתו טמא. עשה בראשו להיות מכה בו טמא. לנוי טהור. ר"א בר צדוק אומר דוד אחד טמא ושני דודין טהור. פרגל שעשה בראשו מסמר להיות מכה בו טמא לנוי טהור.

comments.en: [A metal] comb to which a sting is attached, behold, it is [considered] impure with corpse-impurity. The carpenter’s tongs with which he pulls nails (המסמרים (see GR"A)) is impure. A cup which one put under a door [as a pivot]: Even though it is used with it, it is clean. [If] it became impure and he placed it under the door, it [remains] impure until it is purified. And when is its purification? Beit Shammai say, once it becomes damaged, and Beit Hillel say, once it becomes attached, the words of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says, Beit Shammai say, once it becomes damaged and attached, and Beit Hillel say, once it becomes damaged or attached. Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says, a builder's auger is clean (MS Vienna), for it is only made to be used with the ground. Every tool of a stone-cutter is impure, and the ploughshare is among them. Rabbi Yehuda says, except for the ploughshare. A metal amah [measure] and a leveling rod are impure, and the metzophin (tubes for measuring distances) are pure. A halter is impure because it is like a bridle. Three things on a horse [are impure]: The reins, the bit, and the bridle. The bridle of a horse is impure by itself. [If] a cord or a strap are sewn with it, they are [considered] attached; and knotted, they are not [consided] attached. A teethed strigil and the links of trap, and everything similar on account of being ringed (משום מטבע) [?], behold, they are impure. A teethed strigil that was made inside a house, if it is for sharpening (לחוד), it is impure, and if it is for decoration, it is pure. And if it is in order that a cup or a plate be placed on it, it is impure, because it is [considered to be] like a three-legged table. A lamp-chain is [considered] joined with the comb (see Jastrow (מסרק)). [But] there is no comb that is joined with a ring. The chain of a large bucket must be four handbreadths [to contract impurity], and of a small [bucket], and of those who go up during the pilgrimage festivals, ten [handbreadths]. [If] a rope or a cord was tied to it, whether from above or from below, even one hundred amahs, everything is [considered] attached.
comments.he: מסרק שיש בו דרבן ה"ז טמא <טמא מת>. חולץ של נגר שהוא מוציא בו את המספרים טמא מיניקת שעשאה לתחת הדלת אע"פ שמשתמש בה טהורה. היתה טמאה ועשאה לתחת הדלת טמאה עד שתטהר. ומאימתי טהרתה בית שמאי אומרים משיחבל וב"ה אומרים משיחבר דברי ר"מ ר' יהודה אומר ב"ש אומרים משיחבל ויחבר וב"ה אומרים משיחבל או משיחבר ר' יוסי בר' יהודה אומר קנתור של בנאי שלא נעשה אלא לשמש עם הקרקע. כל כלי הסתת טמאין והערעין עמהם ר' יהודה אומר חוץ מן הערעין. האמה והמחוק של מתכת טמאין והמצופין טהורים אפרומביא טהורה עשה בה שלשלת טמאה. שלשלת שעשאה אפרומביא טמאה מפני שהוא ככלוניס. ג' דברים בסוס השילין והפגר והכולוניס. הכלונס של סוס טמא בפ"ע. המשיחות והרצועות תפורות [בו] חיבור וקשורות אינן חיבור אנדרטין וחוליות של צורה וכל היוצא משום מטבע הרי אלו טמאין. אנדרטין שעשאה בתוך הבית <אם לאור טמא>. אם לנוי טהור. ואם בשביל שיהא נותן עליו את הכוס והקערה טמא מפני שהוא כדולפקי. שלשלת נר חבור על המסרק. אין שם מסרק חבור על הטבעת שלשלת דלי גדול ד' טפחים ושל קטן ושל עולי רגלים עשרה קשר בו חבל או משיחה בין מלמעלה ובין מלמטה אפילו מאה אמה כולו חיבור <אחד>.

sections.en: A staff to the end of which he attached a nail like an axe is susceptible to impurity. If the staff was studded with nails it is susceptible to impurity. Rabbi Shimon ruled: only if he put in three rows. In all cases where he put them in as ornamentation the staff is clean. If he attached a tube to its end, and so also in the case of a door, it is clean. If it was once an independent vessel and then it was fixed to the staff, it remains susceptible to impurity. When does it become pure? Bet Shammai says: when it is damaged; And Bet Hillel says: when it is joined on.
sections.he: מַקֵּל שֶׁעָשָׂה בְרֹאשׁוֹ מַסְמֵר כְּמִין חַזְיָנָא, טָמֵא. סִמְּרוֹ, טָמֵא. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, עַד שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה בוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה סְדָרִים. וְכֻלָּן שֶׁעֲשָׂאָן לְנוֹי, טְהוֹרִין. עָשָׂה בְרֹאשׁוֹ מְנִיקָת, וְכֵן בַּדֶּלֶת, טְהוֹרָה. הָיְתָה כְלִי וְחִבְּרָהּ לוֹ, טְמֵאָה. מֵאֵימָתַי הִיא טָהֳרָתָהּ, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיְּחַבֵּל. בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, מִשֶּׁיְּחַבֵּר:

en: *אנדרטין f. , Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 8, probably אוֹדוֹנְטוֹטִי (ὀδοντωτή, subaudi ξύστρα) a teethed strigil; compare Kelim XIV, 3 מגירה.
דָּקוֹר m. (דקר) chisel or borer. Kelim XIV, 3 ד׳ של חרש the carpenter’s &c.

חֲמוֹר common gender. (Biblical Hebrew; see חָמַר II and
1) [load-carrier, compare גָּמָל.] ass. Niddah 31ᵃ, see גָּרַם. Shabbat 152ᵃ דעל ח׳ וכ׳ he who rides an ass is a freeman. Bava Batra 143ᵃ את וח׳ thou and the ass (shall own my property, a form of donation implying a rational and an irrational being).—Bekhoroth I, 2 ח׳ שילדה וכ׳ if an ass gave birth to &c. Sanhedrin 33ᵃ הלכה חֲמוֹרְךָ וכ׳ thy ass is gone, Tarfon! (I shall have to make compensation for erroneous judgment); and from

—2) (compare various uses of horse) a contrivance for working-men, rest, jack, stocks &c. Kelim XIV, 3 ח׳ של נפחין the smiths’ ass (‘on which the smith sits while using its head as an anvil’, Maimonides; ‘the rest of the bellows’, Rabbenu Shimshon). Ib. XVIII, 3 וח׳ a stand on which the bedstead is placed. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 65, end ח׳ של חרשים carpenters’ sawing-jack (an instrument for torture); Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 70 (alluding to Mishlei XXVII, 22) אפי׳ … בח׳ של חרשים וכ׳ even if you put the wicked man on a carpenter’s jack, you cannot make anything useful out of him (sufferings will have no effect on him); Yalkut Kings 201; Yalkut Mishlei 961; (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Shekalim, p. 15ᵃ במכתש).—plural חֲמוֹרִים. Shabbat 112ᵇ. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 75; and from—Denom. חַמָּר, חִמִּר.—Fem. חֲמוֹרָה. Tosefta Kilayim V, 5.

יָתֵד f. (Biblical Hebrew; compare עתד) [something fastened, driven in,] peg, nail; handle of a tool &c. Yerushalmi Taanit IV, 67ᵈ אשרי אדם … י׳ להיתלות בה (compare Isaiah XXII, 23, sq.) happy the man who has a peg to hang on, i.e. who has a renowned ancestry; ומה היתה יְתֵידָתוֹ וכ׳ and what was R. E.’s. peg?; Yerushalmi Berakhot IV, 7ᵈ top. Gittin 17ᵃ י׳ היא שלא תמוט (my last opinion) is an immovable peg. Megillah 6ᵃ והיא היתה י׳ תקועה וכ׳ and she (Cæsarea) was a peg driven into Israel, i.e. an obnoxious foreign element.—י׳ של מחרישה the pin of the plough. Shabbat XVII, 4; and e, see מַחֲרֵישָׁה.—י׳ האהל tent-pin, see infra.—י׳ הדרכים a way-mark of hardened clay pegs, see גֵּץ; see infra.—plural יְתֵדוֹת, יְתֵידוֹת. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 43 שלשה י׳ גדולות three great pegs (Abraham, Isaac and Jacob). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 62 נתגרו בהן י׳ הארץ the pegs of the land (the remnants of the seven nations, compare Bamidbar XXXIII, 55) arose against them. Kelim XIV, 3 י׳ אהלים י׳ המשוחות Mishnah ed. (Bavli ed. ידות) the (metal) pegs of tents and those of the land measurers. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 7 החרב שפרשה עם י׳ המחרישה the knife (coulter) which has been taken out with the handle of the plough. Mikvaot IX, 2 י׳ הדרכים, explained גץ יוני. Tosefta ib. VI (VII), 14. Bava Kamma 81ᵃ מסתלקין מפני י׳ הד׳ … you may (in walking) turn out from the highway towards the private sidewalk in order to avoid the road-pegs; Yerushalmi Berakhot II, end, 5ᵈ top.

מָשׁוֹחַ m. (מָשַׁח II) surveyor.—plural מָשׁוֹחוֹת. Eruvin IV, 11, see מָצָה. Kelim XIV, 3 יתדות המ׳ the surveyors’ marking pins; שלשלת של מ׳ their measuring chains; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia II, 3 מושיחות.
קַנְטָר m. (see preceding wds.) a pronged tool, bit, or auger. Kelim XIV, 3 הק׳ של בנאי the builder’s ḳanṭar; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 5 קַנְתּוֹר.

שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת f. (שִׁלְשֵׁל II) chain. Kelim XIV, 3. Yerushalmi Taanit II, 65ᵈ הריני עושה לה ש׳ … השַׁלֶּשֶׁת וכ׳ I will make a chain for it (the key), so that if its gets lost, the chain will point it out. Yerushalmi Sukkah V, end, 55ᵈ; Shir HaShirim Rabbah to V, 5 יוחסין(ה) ש׳, see יוֹחָס; ib. introduction שלשת יוחסין. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 97 והש׳ באה כך thus the genealogical chain is continued. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 48 צפה נח (ש)ש׳ האבות וכ׳ Noah foresaw that the genealogical chain of the patriarchs would begin with him (Shem); and from—plural שַׁלְשְׁלָאוֹת, שַׁלְשְׁלָיוֹת. Shabbat 89ᵇ, see רָאָה I. Yerushalmi Ketubot II, 26ᵈ; Yerushalmi Gittin III, 45ᵃ top (among the appurtenances of a siege). Eruvin 58ᵃ; and from

sections.en: A builder's staff and a carpenter's axes are susceptible to impurity. Tent-pegs and surveyors’ pegs are susceptible to impurity. A surveyor's chain is susceptible to impurity, but one used for wood is clean. The chain of a big bucket [is susceptible to impurity to a length of] four handbreadths, and that of a small one [to a length of] ten handbreadths. A blacksmith's jack is susceptible to impurity. A saw whose teeth were made in a hole susceptible to impurity, but if they were turned from below upwards it is clean. All covers are clean except that of a boiler.
sections.he: הַקַּנְטָר שֶׁל בַּנַּאי, וְהַדָּקוֹר שֶׁל חָרָשׁ, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִין. יִתְדוֹת אֹהָלִים וְיִתְדוֹת הַמָּשׁוֹחוֹת, טְמֵאוֹת. שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת שֶׁל מָשׁוֹחוֹת, טְמֵאָה. הָעֲשׂוּיָה לָעֵצִים, טְהוֹרָה. שַׁלְשֶׁלֶת דְּלִי גָדוֹל, אַרְבָּעָה טְפָחִים. וְשֶׁל קָטָן, עֲשָׂרָה. חֲמוֹר שֶׁל נַפָּחִין, טָמֵא. מְגֵרָה שֶׁעָשָׂה שִׁנֶּיהָ בְתוֹךְ הַחוֹר, טְמֵאָה. עֲשָׂאָהּ מִלְּמַטָּן לְמַעְלָן, טְהוֹרָה. וְכָל הַכְּסוּיִן טְהוֹרִים, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל מֵחָם:

en:
כָּנָף (mostly) m.(b. h.; [bend,]
1) wing, wing-feather. Kelim XVII, 14 כְּנַף העוז things made of feathers of the sea-eagle; and e.—Dual כְּנָפַיִם, plural כְּנָפִים, כַּנְפוֹת. Ib. Toharot I, 2. Chullin III, 4 נמרטו כנָפֶיהָ if the wing-feathers are plucked out, see נוֹצָה. Ib. 7 כל שיש לו ארבע כ׳ … וכְנָפָיו וכ׳ … that (locust) which has four feet and four wings …, and whose wings cover the larger portion of its body (is clean); and from

—2) border, lap. Sifré Bamidbar 115 מן הכ׳, see גְּדִילָה II. Ib. מצות כ׳ the law concerning the borders of garments (Bamidbar XV, 38).—plural as ab. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 18; Kohelet Rabbah to XII, 3 (reference. to הראות ib.) אלו כַּנְפֵי הריאה those are the laps (extreme ends) of the lungs. Chullin 45ᵃ עד כנפי ריאה התחתונה to the borders of the lowest lung (of the animal suspended by its feet).—Euphem. for a woman’s lap (pudenda). Yevamot 4ᵃ; 49ᵃ (explained Devarim XXIII, 1) כ׳ שראה אביו the lap which his father has seen, i.e. any woman with whom his father has had sexual connection.

—3) cover. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Zachor, p. 29ᵃ; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 12; Midrash Tanḥuma Ki Thetsé 11 (reference. to יִכָּנֵף, Isaiah XXX, 20) … כל זמן כ׳ מכסה וכ׳ as long as the seed of Amalek survives, it is as if a cover hid the face (of Divinity) &c.

—4) (plural) hands, arms; (of animals) shoulders, fore-legs. Pesachim VII, 11 (84ᵃ) ראשי כ׳ the cartilaginous tops of the fore-legs. Yerushalmi Nazir VI, 55ᶜ bottom of page (reference. to Bamidbar VI, 19) בין שיש לו כ׳ וכ׳ whether or not he has hands (to receive the offerings; Bavli Nazir 46ᵇ כַּפַּיִם). Tosefta Demai II, 11 מקבלין לכ׳ we accept a ḥaber (see חָבֵר), if he promises to observe levitical cleanness of hands; Bekhoroth 30ᵇ. Yerushalmi Demai II, 23ᵃ top מקריבין לכ׳. Ib. כ׳ מדפות וכ׳ the laws concerning hands, &c., see מִדָּף.—אלישע בעל כ׳ one Elisha, a ḥaber observing cleanness of hands. Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 4ᶜ bottom of page; Shabbat 49ᵃ; 130ᵃ (legendary origin of the surname).—Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 32 בעל כ׳ the winged angel.

—5) curved attachments, handles &c. Kelim XI, 6; Tosefta ib. Bava Metzia I, 7, see סִימְפּוֹנְיָא. Kelim XIV, 4 הכ׳ המקבלות וכ׳ the curves on the harness for holding the reins; ib. 5 כ׳ העשוים לנוי for ornament.—Transferred כנפי השכינה or כ׳ divine protection; תחת כ׳ הש׳ under the wings of divine Majesty, i.e. belief and faith in God, Jewish religion. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 2 פושטין … להכניסו תחת כ׳ הש׳ we must reach out a hand to him (the proselyte) in order to take him in &c. Mekhilta Beshalach, Amalek, section (Parashah) 2 לאבד … מתחת כְּנָפֶיךָ to lead thy people away from the faith in thee.—Ruth Rabbah to II, 12; and from

מַחֲגָר m. (חָגַר) the rope around the neck of the animal tied to the wagon (Hai G. and oth.); [the pin fastening the yoke to the pole to prevent the wagon from vacillating (being חִגּר), Maimonides]. Kelim XIV, 4.
סוֹמֶךְ m. (סָמַךְ) the pin for attaching the pole to the wagon, Maimonides; [the ring (ס) suspended from the yoke and pulled over the front end of the pole, R. Hai G. and Arukh) Kelim XIV, 4.

עִינְבּוֹל, עִינְבָּל, עִנְ׳ m. (diminutive of עֵנָב; see אִנְבּוֹל) clapper of a bell. Kelim XIV, 4 ענבול ed. Dehr. (ed. ענבל). Shabbat 58ᵇ עינבל; and from—plural עִינְכּוֹלִין, עִינְבָּלִין, עִנְ׳. Ib. ניטלו עִינְבָּלֵיהֶן if their clappers are gone; (Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia I, 13 אנבילים, אנביליהן, see אִנְבּוֹל).—[Bekhoroth 39ᵇ, see preceding]

עוֹל m. (Biblical Hebrew עֹל; עָלַל) yoke; also pole of a wagon. Kilayim II, 6 מלא הע׳ השרוני the width of the yoke (the team) used in the plain of Sharon. Kelim XIV, 4 הע׳ של מתכות a metal pole (see Maimonides and l.); ib. 5 הע׳ המצופה the metal-tipped pole. Sifré Bamidbar 123 בע׳ שלא לעבודה וכ׳ the text speaks of a yoke not put on for working. Sotah 46ᵃ ע׳ פוסל בין בשעת וכ׳ the bearing of a yoke disqualifies the animal for the ceremony, whether it was put on at working time &c.; and from—Transferred obligation, dependence. Pirkei Avot III, 5 כל המקבל עליו ע׳ תורה … ע׳ מלכות וע׳ דרך ארץ whosoever takes upon himself the yoke (obligations) of the Law, from him shall be removed the yoke of government (oppression) and the yoke of worldly affairs; וכל הפורק ממנו ע׳ תורה וכ׳ but he who throws off the yoke of the Law, will be made to feel the yoke of &c. Berakhot II, 2 כדי שיקבל עליו ע׳ מלכות שמים … ע׳ מצות in order that he may acknowledge his dependence on divine government first (by reciting Devarim VI, 4 sq., see שְׁמַע) and then his subjection to religious duties (by reciting Devarim XI, 13 sq.); and from—plural) עוּלִּין. Midrash Tanḥuma V’zoth 5 שני ע׳ וכ׳ thou puttest two yokes upon thy children; Yalkut Devarim 952.
קַטְרֵב m. a cross-piece in front of yoked animals; [oth. opinion, see Kohelet Arukh Compl. section (Parashah) see: the pin fastening the ropes of the yokes to the pole]. Kelim XIV, 4. Ib. XXI, 2.

תַּמְחוּי common gender. (denominative of מִחְיָה)
1) a plate for various dishes or portions, tray. Kelim XVI, 1, see מַזְנוֹן. Nedarim IV, 4 אוכל … אבל לא מן הת׳ he may eat at the same table with him, but not from the same plate; אבל … מן הת׳ החוזר but he may eat with him from a plate which goes back to the host (each time a guest is served). Ma'asrot I, 7 נותן … ולת׳ he may put the oil on the cake (חֲמִיטָה) or on the plate. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia VIII, end, 11ᵈ השאילני תַּמְחוּיְיךָ וכ׳ (or תַּמְחוּיֶיךָ, plural) lend me thy plate and dine with me; and from—Esp. tamḥuy, charity plate, daily distributed food collected from contributors, soup-kitchen, contradistinguished to קוּפָּה, see as well Peah VIII, 7 מי … לא יטול מן הת׳ he who has the means for two meals, must not accept support from the tamḥuy. Bava Batra 8ᵇ ת׳ נגבית בשלשה וכ׳ the tamḥuy is collected under the supervision of three persons, and distributed by three persons, for the mode of its collection and distribution is the same; ת׳ לעניי העולם וכ׳ the ṭ. is for all poor people wherever they may come from, the ḳuppah for the town poor only. Pesachim X, 1 אפילו מן הת׳ even if he is supported from the ṭ.; Yerushalmi ib. 37ᵇ bottom of page; and from—plural תַּמְחוּיִין. Yerushalmi Terumot VIII, 45ᵈ top. Keritot 12ᵇ ת׳ מחלקין (not מחולקין) trays form a separation, i.e. if one eats two half-olive sizes of forbidden food from two different plates, they are not counted together as one olive-size; Shabbat 71ᵃ; Yerushalmi ib. VII, 9ᵇ; and from

—2) (from its shape) the partition in a wagon for freight or baggage, Maimonides; (a cavity in the yoke, Rabbenu Shimshon).—plural תַּמְחוּיוֹת. Kelim XIV, 4.

comments.en: Rings fashioned to receive straps -- behold, they are pure, for they are only made for decorative purposes. [But if] they were made to weigh down the straps, or so that the straps are suspended from them, they are impure. An iron [ring] that is under the neck of an animal, or on top of the neck of an animal. § A nail with which one connects a wheel so that it does not slip is impure, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel renders it pure. In this regard, Rabbi Yehuda agrees with the Sages: With regard to metal traveling box that one made into a mirror, and it broke and its utility ceased, it is pure (alt., "impure" (GR"A)). And the Sages say, either way, it is impure. A mirror that is broken: If it can still be used for its initial purpose, it is impure, [and] if not, it is pure. [If] it was scratched: If it still reflects the majority of one's face, it is impure, and if not, it is pure.
comments.he: הטבעות המקבלות את הרצועות הרי אלו טהורות שאינן עשויות אלא לנוי. העשויות להכביד את הרצועות ושהרצועות תלויות בהן טמאות. ברזל שתחת צואר בהמה ושעל גבי צואר בהמה טמא. מסמר שהוא מחבר בו את הגלגל שלא ישמט טמאה ורבן שמעון בן גמליאל מטהר בזה מודה ר' יהודה לחכמים בכסוי טני של מתכת שעשה בו מראה נשבר ובטל מתשמישו טהור וחכ"א בין כך ובין כך טמא. מראה שנשברה אם משמשת מעין מלאכתה ראשונה טמאה אם לאו טהורה. נטשטשה אם מראה רוב הפנים טמאה ואם לאו טהורה.

sections.en: The parts of a wagon that are susceptible to impurity: the metal yoke, the cross-bar, the side-pieces that hold the straps, the iron bar under the necks of the cattle, the pole-pin, the metal girth, the trays, the clapper, the hook, and any nail that holds any of its parts together.

VII, 10ᶜ bottom of page השף את העור על גבי העמוד. Kelim XXX, 1 שָׁפָן בשופין files them with a file. 1) to be rubbed off, made smooth, level. Tosefta Bava Kamma X, 4 מטבע ונ׳ if he took by force a coin, and it became rubbed off (effaced).

—2) to be ground, crushed. Tosefta Bava Metzia XI, 8 מוציא אדם זבלו … כדי שיִישּׁוֹף וכ׳ a man may take out his material for dung and place it in front of his house, that it may be stamped upon by the feet of man and beast; Bava Kamma 30ᵃ; 81ᵇ; Bava Metzia 118ᵇ כדי שיהא נישוף. 1) to crush. —Part. pass. שָׁפוּי, plural שְׁפוּיִין crushed, humble, contrite (= Biblical Hebrew דַּכָּא). Tosefta Chagigah II, 9 עניו וש׳ humble and contrite; Tosefta Sanhedrin VII, 1 וש׳ (only); Yerushalmi ib. I, 19ᶜ. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 60 דווין וש׳ Arukh (ed. ושפופין) broken down and crushed (poor); and e.

—2) to rub, smooth, plane. —Part. pass. as ab. a) smooth. Piël - שִׁפָּה, שִׁי׳
1) to plane, saw, trim. Chullin 125ᵃ קולית שש׳ וכ׳ a thigh-bone which one sawed through lengthwise. Pirkei Avot Zar. 42ᵃ ישראל שש׳ ע"ז וכ׳ if an Israelite chipped off an idol whether for his own purpose (to use the wood) or for its sake (to improve its appearance). Ib. 49ᵇ. Yerushalmi Gittin V, 47ᵃ bottom of page גזלו ושִׁיפָּהוּ if he took a block by force and planed it. —2) to smooth, polish, Kelim XIV, 5 משׁיְשַׁפֶּנּוּ Arukh; Nedarim 56ᵇ משׁיְשַׁפֵּם, see שׁוּף II.—Transferred to pacify, give satisfaction. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia V, 10ᵇ המבטל … חייב לשַׁפּוֹת לו if a tenant or an agent neglects his neighbor’s field, he must indemnify him; ib. IX, beginning 12ᵃ

—3) to leave smooth places, (compare חָלַק Hifil) to plant wide apart. Yerushalmi Orlah I, beginning 60ᶜ לקורות במְשַׁפֶּה (or במַשְׁפֶּה Hifil) when he plants the trees wide apart, it is an indication that he wants to raise them for beams, opposed רָצַף. Bava Batra V, 4 הגדילו לא יְשַׁפֶּה (or יַשְׁפֶּה) if they (the trees bought in a person’s field) grew large, he (the owner of the field) has no right to smooth the field (cut the trees down). Ib. הגדילו ישפה when they are grown large, he (the owner of the trees) may cut them (in order to use the ground they occupy); and e.

And with regard to the essence of Rabbi Yoḥanan’s statement, the Gemara asks: And does Rabbi Yoḥanan not require that the vessel’s new usage must be of the same type as the original labor in order for it to retain its ritual impurity after it has undergone change? Wasn’t it taught in a baraita: “Every bed on which a zav is lying is ritually impure and every vessel on which he is sitting shall be ritually impure” (Leviticus 15:4). I might have thought, based on this verse, that if one overturned a vessel the size of a se’a and sat on it, or overturned a vessel the size of a half-se’a [tarkav] and sat on it, the vessel would become ritually impure. Therefore, the verse states: On which the zav is sitting, i.e., that which is designated for sitting, excluding that vessel with regard to which one says to the zav: Stand and we will perform our labor with the vessel. In that case, because the vessel is primarily used for purposes other than sitting, it does not become ritually impure even when the zav sits on it.

There is a dispute between the amora’im on this matter: Rabbi Elazar says: With regard to ritual impurity imparted by treading [midras], i.e., the halakhot pertaining to a zav or to a menstruating woman who sits or lies down on an object, one states the principle: Stand and we will perform our labor to maintain the purity of the vessel. However, one does not state with regard to one who is ritually impure due to a corpse: Stand and we will perform our labor to maintain the purity of the vessel. In other words, an object that became ritually impure through contact with a corpse and was subsequently broken, since it is possible to use it for some other purpose, it remains a vessel and susceptible to ritual impurity. However, Rabbi Yoḥanan said: Even with regard to one who is ritually impure due to a corpse, one states the principle: Stand and we will perform our labor to maintain the purity of the vessel. According to his opinion, a vessel that is no longer suited for its initial use, even though it serves another purpose, is considered broken. Therefore, the bell, since it is no longer suited for ringing, remains ritually pure according to Rabbi Yoḥanan’s opinion, even though it remains suited for drinking water.

The Gemara answers: Reverse the opinions in the first dispute: It was not Rabbi Yoḥanan who gave that reason; it was Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina. The Gemara asks: And what did you see that led you to reverse the first? Reverse the opinions of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar in the latter dispute, and avoid a contradiction in the statements of Rabbi Yoḥanan in that way.

The Gemara answers: That is because we learned elsewhere that Rabbi Yoḥanan requires that the vessel’s new use will be of the same type as the original labor. His opinion here is consistent with his opinion there. As it was taught in a baraita: The shoe of an animal, if it is made of metal, can become ritually impure. The Gemara asks: For what use by people is it suited? Vessels designated for animal use do not become ritually impure unless they have some use for people. Rav said: It is suited for use as a vessel from which one could drink water in war when there are no other available vessels. And Rabbi Ḥanina said: It is suited for use as a vessel from which one could smear oil on his body during a war. And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: When he flees from the battlefield he places it on his foot and runs over thorns and the thistles. Apparently, the only use for the shoe of an animal that would render it capable of becoming ritually impure when used by a person is use of the same type as the original labor.

The Gemara asks parenthetically: What is the practical difference between the explanation of Rav and that of Rabbi Ḥanina? The Gemara answers: There is a practical difference between them in a case where the sandal is repulsive and dirty. In Rav’s opinion, since one would not drink water from it, it cannot become ritually impure. According to Rabbi Ḥanina, since one could still use it to spread oil on his body, it can become ritually impure.

What is the practical difference between the explanation of Rabbi Yoḥanan and that of Rabbi Ḥanina? There is a practical difference between them in a case where the shoe is heavy. It is suited for spreading oil; it is not suited for one to place on his foot. Therefore, it cannot become ritually impure according to Rabbi Yoḥanan.
he: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא בָּעֵי מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה רִאשׁוֹנָה? וְהָתַנְיָא: ״וְכׇל כְּלִי אֲשֶׁר יֵשֵׁב עָלָיו וְגוֹ׳״ — יָכוֹל כָּפָה סְאָה וְיָשַׁב עָלֶיהָ, כָּפָה תַּרְקַב וְיָשַׁב עָלֶיהָ יְהֵא טָמֵא, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר יֵשֵׁב עָלָיו הַזָּב״ — מִי שֶׁמְיוּחָד לִישִׁיבָה, יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאוֹמְרִים לוֹ: עֲמוֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ.

רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: בְּמִדְרָסוֹת אוֹמְרִים ״עֲמוֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ״, וְאֵין אוֹמְרִים בִּטְמֵא מֵת ״עֲמוֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ״. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף אוֹמֵר בִּטְמֵא מֵת ״עֲמוֹד וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְלַאכְתֵּנוּ״.
אֵיפוֹךְ קַמַּיְיתָא. וּמַאי חֲזֵית דְּאָפְכַתְּ קַמַּיְיתָא? אֵיפוֹךְ בָּתְרָיְיתָא!

הָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּבָעֵי מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה רִאשׁוֹנָה. דְּתַנְיָא: סַנְדָּל שֶׁל בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת טָמֵא. לְמַאי חֲזֵי? אָמַר רַב: רָאוּי לִשְׁתּוֹת בּוֹ מַיִם בַּמִּלְחָמָה. וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: רָאוּי לָסוּךְ בּוֹ שֶׁמֶן בַּמִּלְחָמָה. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁבּוֹרֵחַ מִן הַקְּרָב מַנִּיחוֹ בְּרַגְלָיו וְרָץ עַל קוֹצִין וְעַל הַבַּרְקָנִים.
מַאי בֵּין רַב לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא? אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דִּמְאִיס.
בֵּין רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא? אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּיַקִּיר.

sections.en: The clean parts of a wagon are the following: the yoke that is only plated [with metal], side-pieces made for ornamentation, tubes that give out a noise, the lead at the side of the necks of the cattle, the rim of the wheel, the plates and mountings, and all other nails, all of these are clean. Metal shoes of cattle are susceptible to impurity but those made of cork are clean. When does a sword become susceptible to impurity? When it has been polished. And a knife? When it has been sharpened.
sections.he: הַטְּהוֹרִין שֶׁבָּעֲגָלָה, הָעֹל הַמְצֻפֶּה, כְּנָפַיִם הָעֲשׂוּיוֹת לְנוֹי, וּשְׁפוֹפָרוֹת הַמַּשְׁמִיעוֹת אֶת הַקּוֹל, וְהָאֲבָר שֶׁבְּצַד צַוְּארֵי בְהֵמָה, הַסּוֹבֵב שֶׁל גַּלְגַּל, הַטַּסִּים, וְהַצִּפּוּיִים, וּשְׁאָר כָּל הַמַּסְמְרוֹת, טְהוֹרִין. סַנְדְּלֵי בְהֵמָה שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת, טְמֵאִין. שֶׁל שַׁעַם, טְהוֹרִין. הַסַּיִף מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבֵּל טֻמְאָה, מִשֶּׁיְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ. וְהַסַּכִּין, מִשֶּׁיַשְׁחִיזֶנָּה:

en:
מַרְאָה f. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding)
1) mirror. Kelim XIV, 6 שעשה בו מ׳ (not שעשאה) one part of which he polished to serve as a mirror. Tosefta Shabbat XIII (XIV), 16; and from—plural מַרְאוֹת. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 4 מ׳ גדולות magnifying mirrors; מ׳ קטנות diminishing mirrors; and e.

—2) picture.—plural as ab. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 73 היה לך מ׳ בתוך ביתך didst thou have pictures in thy house? שחורה … או לבנה of black persons or of white?

sections.en: A metal basket-cover which was turned into a mirror: Rabbi Judah rules that it is clean. And the sages rule that it is susceptible to impurity. A broken mirror, if it does not reflect the greater part of the face, is clean.
sections.he: כְּסוּי טֶנִי שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת שֶׁעָשָׂה בוֹ מַרְאָה, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר, וַחֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין. מַרְאָה שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרָה, אִם אֵינָהּ מַרְאָה אֶת רֹב הַפָּנִים, טְהוֹרָה:

en: Rabbi Eliezer says, a metal vessel that became impure and [then] was broken and melted down: He sprinkles [the waters of purification] upon it that same day and [sprinkles] a second time on the fourth day. And [a metal vessel] that became impure and he sprinkled upon it and it [then] broke and he melted it down, [he sprinkles] a second time upon it that same day. Rabbi Yehoshua says, one may not sprinkle any less than on the third and the seventh day. Rabbi Natan says, Rabbi Eliezer says, a metal vessel that became impure and was broken and melted down, and he sprinkled upon it, and it was broken and melted down and [he sprinkled] a second time upon it that same day [is pure], [and] Rabbi Yehoshua says, one may not sprinkle any less than on the third and the seventh day.

A knee-shaped (jointed) key that was broken inside its joint: Rabbi Meir renders it impure and Rabbi Yehuda renders it pure, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says, their words should be switched (and see Kel. 14:8, switching them). A mustard-strainer that became separated along its length is pure. Along its width: If it is [still] useful for its original purpose, it is impure, and if not, it is pure. Said Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok, Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree about a mustard strainer as to which three bottom holes broke, one next to the other (i.e., forming one large hole), that it is pure. About what did they disagree? About two: That Beit Shammai renders it impure and Beit Hillel renders it pure. A jug whose mouth one intends to reforge and make it like a tube is only impure once he reforges the mouth.
he: רבי אליעזר אומר כלי מתכת שנטמא ונשבר והתיכו מזה עליו בו ביום ושונה עליו ברביעי ושנטמא והזה עליו ונשבר והתיכו שונה עליו בו ביום ר' יהושע אומר אין הזאה פחות משלישי ושביעי ר' נתן אומר ר' אליעזר אומר כלי מתכת שנטמא ונשבר והתיכו והזה עליו ונשבר והתיכו ושנה עליו בו ביום ר' יהושע אומר אין הזאה פחות משלישי ושביעי.

מפתח של רכובה שנשבר מתוך רכובתו ר"מ מטמא ורבי יהודה מטהר ורבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר חילוף הדברים. מסננת של חרדל שנחלקה לארכה טהורה. לרחבה. אם משמשת מעין מלאכתה ראשונה טמאה. ואם לאו טהורה. א"ר אלעזר בר' צדוק לא נחלקו בית שמאי ובית הלל על מסננת של חרדל שנפרצו בה שלשה נקבין מלמטה זה בצד זה שהיא טהורה על מה נחלקו על שנים שבית שמאי מטמאין ובית הלל מטהרין קיתון שהוא עתיד לטפוח על פיו ולעשותו כצינור <טהור> [טמא] עד שיטפח את פיו.

sections.en: Metal vessels remain unclean and become clean even when broken, the words of Rabbi Eliezer. Rabbi Joshua says: they can be made clean only when they are whole. How so? If they were sprinkled upon and on the same day they were broken and then they were recast and sprinkled upon on the same day, they are clean, the words of Rabbi Eliezer. Rabbi Joshua says: there can be no effective sprinkling earlier than on the third and the seventh day.
sections.he: כְּלֵי מַתָּכוֹת מִטַּמְּאִין וּמִטַּהֲרִין שְׁבוּרִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, אֵינָן מִטַּהֲרִין אֶלָּא שְׁלֵמִין. כֵּיצַד, הִזָּה עֲלֵיהֶן, נִשְׁבְּרוּ בוֹ בַיּוֹם, הִתִּיכָן וְחָזַר וְהִזָּה עֲלֵיהֶן שֵׁנִית בּוֹ בַיּוֹם, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר, אֵין הַזָּיָה פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלִישִׁי וּשְׁבִיעִי:

en:
אַרְכּוּבָה f. (רכב)
1) the leg from under the hip-bone to the ankle, the knee and its surrounding parts (containing three sections each of which is called א׳ and defined by a different surname). Chullin IV, 6; see ib. 76ᵃ (also רְכוּבָה); and from

—2) anything joined, joint. Kilayim VII, 1 הא׳ שבגפן (Tosefta ib. IV, 11, Variant הבריכה שבסלע) that part of the vine which is bent down and laid in the ground to rise at another place. Yerushalmi Megillah I, 71ᶜ bottom of page א׳ של למ"ד the lower joint of the Lammed. Kelim XIV, 8 מפתח של א׳ וכ׳ (Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 15 רוֹכְבָּה … רְכוּבָתוֹ) a key with a joint, broken at the joint.—plural אַרְכּוּבוֹת. Niddah 30ᵇ. Bava Metzia 105ᵃ
אַרְפְּכָס, (אֲפַרְכָּס) m. (ἅρπαξ = ὑδράρπαξ, ἁρπάγιον) clepsydra, water-clock. Kelim XIV, 8; XXX, 4 אר׳ Arukh (ed. אפ׳). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 4 הבא אר׳ get me a clepsydra.

גַּם II, גַּאַם, (גמא) m. (preceding) joint, angle, especially two sides of a rectangle. Eruvin 55ᵃ כמין גם Arukh (ed. גאם) in the shape of a right angle. Zevachim 53ᵇ גמא (Yalkut Vayikra 441 גאם). Pesachim 8ᵇ שורה אחת כמין ג׳ one row of wine vessels, in the shape of &c., i.e. the front and the whole upper layer. Yerushalmi ib. I, 27ᵇ bottom of page קולפו כמין גם.—Kelim XIV, 8 (מפתח) של גם שנשבר מתוך גומו a key whose bit is joined (opposed to של ארכובה of one piece) broken at its junction. [Shabbat 105ᵃ על הגם Arukh, ed. על הגַּס, see as well]—plural גַּמִּים, גַּמִּין. Yerushalmi Pesachim l. common gender. קולפו כמין שני ג׳ he takes off for examination two front and two upper layers, see supra. Ib. if the vessels are arranged like steps קולפו ג׳ ג׳ he must examine by front and upper layers on each landing. Bava Metzia 28ᵃ מדת גַּמָּיו the combined measure of both dimensions of a piece of goods, square measure, opposed מדת ארכו ומדת רחבו the measure of each dimension specified.—Shabbat 103ᵇ גַּמִּין, see גי"מל.—[Commentators explain our word = Greek Gamma, Γ, whence the Variant גַּמָּא.]

חָף m. (compare Biblical Hebrew חֹף; חפף I)
1) border, shore. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 13 (reference. to Bamidbar VII, 26) אין כף אלא חף וכ׳ Kaf (bowl) means the same as ḥaf (shore), as it is said (Psalms XCVIII, 8) rivers strike the Kaf.

—2) (compare חִיפָּא) [rim, ridge,] ward of a lock (פותחת); bit of a key (corresponding to the ward); pivot of a door (see Smith, Dictionary of Greek and Roman Antiquities, Third American Edition, New-York 1858 section (Parashah) vv. Cardo, Clavis). Shabbat VIII, 6 כדי … חף bone large enough to make of it a ḥaf; explained ib. 81ᵃ חַפֵּי פותחת the rims (ward) of a lock; Yerushalmi ib. 11ᵇ bot מהו חף סרגיד what ḥaf is meant? (Answ.) the key-ward; ib. תמן היא עביד חף בלוט וכ׳ (not כלוט) there (Kelim XIV, 8) he (R. Judah) uses ḥaf in the sense of a key-bit, and here (Shabbat l. common gender.) in the sense of a key-ward.

—3) the border of a web, used for starting a new web by fastening the warp to it. Yerushalmi ib. VII, 10ᶜ, see נִיר IV.—plural חַפִּים, חַפִּין. Kelim XIII, 6 פותחת של עץ וח׳ וכ׳ if the lock is of wood and its key-bits of metal (ed. Dehr. חָפִין). Ib. XIV, 8 ניטלו ח׳ if the teeth of the bit are broken off (damaged). Shabbat 81ᵃ, see supra. Yerushalmi ib. IV, 7ᵃ top חַפֵּי לסוטות borders used for weaving veils. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to III, 10 (explained פתות, I Kings VII, 50) חפיפות, read: חַפֵּי פותחות the pivots; (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 6 בלוטין שבפותחות, see בָּלוּט).—Kelim XI, 4 הַפִּין = החפין.

מַפְתֵּחַ, מַפְתֵּיחַ common gender. (Biblical Hebrew; key. Kelim XIV, 8, see אַרְכּוּבָה. Bech. 45ᵃ. Taanit 2ᵃ, sq.; and from—plural מַפְתֵּחוֹת, מַפְתֵּיחוֹת. Tamid III, 6. Taanit l. common gender.; and from

סָתַם (Biblical Hebrew; = סחתם, Saf. of חתם)
1) to stop up, close, shut. Pirkei Avot Zar. V, 3 כדי שישתום ויִסְתּוֹם ויגוב, see נָגַב. Bava Metzia VII, 5 שלא יהא … ויהא סוֹתֵם את הפתח וכ׳ that he (the laborer) must not be greedy so as to shut the door before himself (make himself objectionable to employers). Chullin 43ᵃ, and e. מרה שניקבה וכבד סוֹתַמְתָּהּ if the bladder of the gall is perforated, and the liver (adhering to the perforated spot) closes it up. Ib. 49ᵇ חלב טהור סותם clean fat (such as it is permitted to eat) forms a stopper (to an adjacent organ, and makes the animal so affected permitted). Pesachim IV, 9 (56ᵃ) ס׳ מי גיחון וכ׳ he stopped up the water of the upper Gihon (II Chr. XXXII, 3); and from—Part. pass. סָתוּם; f. סְתוּמָה; plural סְתוּמִים, סְתוּמִין; סְתוּמוֹת. Yevamot 71ᵇ; Niddah 30ᵇ; Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 14 נפתח הס׳ ונסתם וכ׳ the organ which (in the embryonic stage) was closed, opens, and that which was open, closes itself. Beitzah IV, 3 בית … ס׳ a room filled with fruit which was closed up (with bricks). Yerushalmi ib. 62ᶜ bottom of page לפסים ס׳ pots with their lids on (not yet cut apart); Tosefta ib. III, 13; Tosefta Shabbat XVI (XVII), 13. Sanhedrin 94ᵃ (reference. to לסרבה, Isaiah IX, 6) מפני מה כל מ"ם … וזה ס׳ why is every Mem in the middle of a word open, and this one is closed (final Mem). Megillah 3ᵃ פתוחין … וס׳ בסוף וכ׳ open in the middle of words and closed at the end (see מנצפ"ך); and from—Esp. פרשה סתומה a paragraph in the Torah separated from the preceding by a vacant space in the middle of the line, opposed to פתוחה a section beginning a new indented line. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 96, beginning, see infra. Masechet Sof’rim I, 14 איזוהי ס׳ כל שהניח וכ׳ what is a closed paragraph? When space is left &c.; וכמה יניח … ותהא נקראת ס׳ and how much space must be left …, in order that the paragraph may be called closed?; and from

—2) to conceal. Breishit Rabbah l. common gender. (reference. to the section beginning with Breishit XLVII, 28) that paragraph is closed, שס׳ ממנו וכ׳ because the Lord concealed from his vision all (coming) troubles; (Yalkut ib. 154 שנסתמו ממנו, see infra); and e.—Part. pass. as ab. concealed, not explicitly stated, opposed מפורש. Zevachim 53ᵃ יִלָּמֵד ס׳ מן המפורש let that which is not explicitly stated in a law be derived (by analogy) from what is explicitly stated; Sifra Aḥăré, beginning יְלַמֵּד פתוח על הס׳ let the explicit statement throw light on the implicit. Megillah 15ᵃ כל … אבותיו ס׳ a person (mentioned in the Bible) whose deeds and the deeds of whose ancestors are not stated; and from—Yerushalmi Beitzah l. common gender. (in Chald. dict.) סתומה the anonymous opinion, see סְתָמָא.

Nifal - נִסְתַּם,

Hithpaël - הִסְתַּתֵּם, , Nithpaël נִסְתַּתֵּם to be closed; to be concealed; to be silenced. Breishit Rabbah l. common gender. בקש … ונ׳ ממנו Jacob wanted to reveal the end of the captivity, and it was closed before him; Yalkut ib. l. common gender. נִסְתְּמוּ ממנו, see supra. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to I, 4 היה אומר … ומִסְתַּתְּמִין he said a word (of charm) over them, and they became silent (dumb). Sanhedrin 31ᵇ לעולם … עד שיִסְתַּתֵּם טענותיו (Hilkhot Rabbeinu Alfasi שיִסְתּוֹם; Asheri שיסתיר) he may continually bring evidence and refute, until he declares himself closed as to his pleas, i.e., until he declares that he has no more evidence to offer. Yevamot 76ᵃ; Tosefta ib. X, 4, and e. נ׳ כשר if the perforation in the membrum has closed itself again, he is considered unblemished. Kelim XIV, 8 נִסְתַּתְּמוּ נקבין if the holes have been stopped up. Sanhedrin 94ᵃ לכך נ׳ therefore the Mem was closed (the final מ was written). Sotah 13ᵇ נסתתמו ממנו שערי וכ׳ the gates of wisdom were closed before him (he lost his judicial judgment); and e.

Piël - סִיתֵּם to close. Yerushalmi Sanhedrin X, 28ᶜ bottom of page היו … מְסַתְּמִין וכ׳ the ministering angels closed the windows (of heaven) that the prayer of Manasseh might not rise; Devarim Rabbah section (Parashah) 2; (Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Shub., p. 162ᵇ סוֹתְמִין).

comments.en: A knee-shaped (jointed) key that was broken inside its joint: Rabbi Meir renders it impure and Rabbi Yehuda renders it pure, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamaliel says, their words should be switched (and see Kel. 14:8, switching them). A mustard-strainer that became separated along its length is pure. Along its width: If it is [still] useful for its original purpose, it is impure, and if not, it is pure. Said Rabbi Elazar bar Tzadok, Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree about a mustard strainer as to which three bottom holes broke, one next to the other (i.e., forming one large hole), that it is pure. About what did they disagree? About two: That Beit Shammai renders it impure and Beit Hillel renders it pure. A jug whose mouth one intends to reforge and make it like a tube is only impure once he reforges the mouth.
comments.he: מפתח של רכובה שנשבר מתוך רכובתו ר"מ מטמא ורבי יהודה מטהר ורבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר חילוף הדברים. מסננת של חרדל שנחלקה לארכה טהורה. לרחבה. אם משמשת מעין מלאכתה ראשונה טמאה. ואם לאו טהורה. א"ר אלעזר בר' צדוק לא נחלקו בית שמאי ובית הלל על מסננת של חרדל שנפרצו בה שלשה נקבין מלמטה זה בצד זה שהיא טהורה על מה נחלקו על שנים שבית שמאי מטמאין ובית הלל מטהרין קיתון שהוא עתיד לטפוח על פיו ולעשותו כצינור <טהור> [טמא] עד שיטפח את פיו.

sections.en: A knee-shaped key that was broken off at the knee is clean. Rabbi Judah says that it is unclean because one can open with it from within. A gamma-shaped key that was broken off at its shorter arm is clean. If it retained the teeth and the gaps it remains unclean. If the teeth were missing it is still unclean on account of the gaps; if the gaps were blocked up it is unclean on account of the teeth. If the teeth were missing and the gaps were blocked up, or if they were merged into one another, it is clean. If in a mustard-strainer three holes in its bottom were merged into one another the strainer is clean. A metal mill-funnel is unclean.
sections.he: מַפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל אַרְכֻּבָּה שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּר מִתּוֹךְ אַרְכֻּבָּתוֹ, טָהוֹר, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַמֵּא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא פוֹתֵחַ בּוֹ מִבִּפְנִים. וְשֶׁל גַּם שֶׁנִּשְׁבַּר מִתּוֹךְ גֻּמּוֹ, טָהוֹר. הָיוּ בוֹ חָפִין וּנְקָבִין, טָמֵא. נִטְּלוּ חָפִין, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי נְקָבִין. נִסְתַּתְּמוּ נְקָבִין, טָמֵא מִפְּנֵי חָפִין. נִטְּלוּ חָפִין וְנִסְתַּתְּמוּ נְקָבִין, אוֹ שֶׁפָּרְצוּ זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה, טָהוֹר. מְסַנֶּנֶת שֶׁל חַרְדָּל שֶׁנִּפְרְצוּ בָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה נְקָבִים מִלְּמַטָּן זֶה לְתוֹךְ זֶה, טְהוֹרָה. וְהָאֲפַרְכֵּס שֶׁל מַתָּכוֹת, טְמֵאָה:
